seoTitle: Change Your Hostinger Domain Name for Free
metaDescription: Update the domain name attached to your Hostinger website through hPanel, with a warning about email data before you start.
intro: Rebranding a project or swapping a placeholder domain for the real one doesn't require a new hosting plan on Hostinger. You can point your existing website at a new domain name from inside hPanel in a few clicks. The one catch is that the switch resets anything tied to the old domain, including your email inboxes and any backups, so it pays to know exactly what the confirmation screen is telling you before you click through it. This guide follows the process screen by screen: finding the setting, reading the warning correctly, and completing the change.
prerequisites: The new domain name already registered, either through Hostinger or another registrar. A domain bought through Hostinger shows up automatically in the change-domain picker; one bought elsewhere still works, but you type it in manually and it needs to be pointed at Hostinger's nameservers to actually resolve once the change is made.
costNote: Changing the domain attached to a site costs nothing by itself; it's a setting inside hPanel, not a paid add-on. The only real cost is the new domain's registration if you don't already own one.

steps.heading: Log in and open the Websites list
steps.body: Go to Hostinger's website and use the login button in the top right to sign in with your account email and password; the login form has a reset link if you've forgotten it. Hostinger drops you straight into hPanel, the control panel where every hosting, domain, and email setting for your account lives. The left sidebar is the main navigation for the rest of this process: Websites, Domains, Emails, and Billing all sit here.

image.caption: The hPanel home screen after logging in, with the sidebar (Websites, Domains, Emails) running down the left side.

steps.heading: Open Websites and find the right site
steps.body: Click Websites in the sidebar to see every site attached to your hosting account, each listed with its current domain, plan, and quick-action buttons for tools, WP Admin, and its dashboard. If you manage more than one site, use the search bar at the top to filter by domain or name instead of scrolling the full list. Confirm you've found the correct entry before continuing, since the domain change only applies to the site you select here.

image.caption: The Websites list in hPanel, showing every site on the account with its own row of management options.

steps.heading: Open the three-dot menu and select Change domain
steps.body: Each website row ends with a three-dot icon that opens a menu of extra actions: Add to favorites, Add tag, Change domain, Website Details, and Delete. Click Change domain. If the site is still running on a temporary Hostinger-assigned address, you'll also see a banner right on the row itself reading "Current domain is temporary," with the same Change domain link; either path gets you to the same place.

image.caption: The three-dot menu on a website row, with Change domain listed alongside Website Details and Delete.

steps.heading: Read the warning and confirm you understand it
steps.body: This is the step that trips people up. The Change Website's Domain dialog spells out three consequences before it lets you proceed: your email plan resets and mailboxes on the current domain are deleted, associated subdomains are removed, and existing website backups tied to the current domain are lost and can't be restored. Hostinger's own support documentation confirms all three in plain terms. Export any email you need and note down anything backup-related before you tick the checkbox confirming you understand; there's no undo once you click Change.

image.caption: The Change Website's Domain confirmation dialog, listing exactly what gets reset: email, subdomains, and backups, before you can proceed.

steps.heading: Enter your new domain and finish the switch
steps.body: After confirming, you're prompted to enter the new domain name; pick it from the dropdown if it was bought through Hostinger, or type it in if it's registered elsewhere. Enter it carefully; a typo here means repeating the whole process. Click Next to complete the change. Hostinger's documentation puts nameserver propagation at up to 24 hours, often faster, though a full worldwide update can occasionally run longer, so don't panic if the new address doesn't resolve everywhere immediately. If it still looks wrong after a day, contact Hostinger's support team to check the DNS records on their end.

troubleshooting.problem: The new domain doesn't load the site after the change completes
troubleshooting.cause: A domain bought outside Hostinger isn't automatically pointed at Hostinger's nameservers; the in-panel Change Domain action updates the website's record, but the domain itself still needs its nameservers set at the registrar.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the domain's DNS/nameserver settings in hPanel and point it to Hostinger's nameservers if that hasn't been done, then allow up to 24 hours for propagation.

troubleshooting.problem: Email accounts on the old domain are gone after switching
troubleshooting.cause: This is expected, not a bug. Hostinger's confirmation dialog and support documentation both state the email plan resets and mailboxes tied to the previous domain are deleted as part of the change.
troubleshooting.fix: Recreate the mailboxes you need under the new domain in the Emails section. There's no recovery path for the old ones once the change is confirmed, so back up anything important beforehand.

faq.question: Will changing my domain delete my email data?
faq.answer: Yes. Hostinger's own documentation states that your email plan resets and mailboxes tied to the current domain are deleted, so export anything important before you confirm the change.

faq.question: Are my website files and backups affected?
faq.answer: Existing backups linked to the current domain are lost and can't be restored once you switch. Subdomains attached to the old domain are also removed.

faq.question: Does the new domain need to already be registered?
faq.answer: Yes. A domain bought through Hostinger appears automatically in the picker during the change; one bought elsewhere can be typed in, but it needs to be pointed at Hostinger's nameservers separately for the site to actually load there.

faq.question: How long does it take for the new domain to work everywhere?
faq.answer: Hostinger's documentation puts nameserver propagation at up to 24 hours, often less. Give it that long before assuming something's broken.

faq.question: Where do I find the Change Domain option?
faq.answer: Go to Websites in hPanel, find your site, and click the three-dot icon at the end of its row. Change domain is listed there, and it also appears as a banner link if the site is still on a temporary domain.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in 2025. The email/subdomain/backup warning, the domain-registration prerequisite, and the propagation window were re-checked against Hostinger's official support documentation in September 2026, which tightened the propagation estimate from this guide's original 'a few minutes to a couple of days' to Hostinger's own stated 'up to 24 hours' and added the requirement that a domain bought outside Hostinger still needs its nameservers pointed separately.
